findings.title: Intentional failure/contact is a control prerequisite
findings.finding: C02 needs legally obtainable interruption marks and observable conditional-cast exit state. C03 requires finite deliberate-contact preparation and reserves; a third gesture needs an acquired refill, while ordinary movement remains the no-refill exploitation branch. Neither an always-dodge nor always-accept fallback demonstrates these choices.

findings.title: Withholding must override ordinary offense explicitly
findings.finding: The next attack releases escrow, while moving/guarding do not and timeout still does. Ordinary attack fallback can contradict planned relocation. The authoring obligation includes withholding, pending/admitted action handling and ordinary fallback after settlement; the retort reserve similarly needs a release-versus-wait choice.

assumptions: Only declared cancel windows interrupt admitted actions.
The four-second hold is an untested parameter, not a proven route budget.

findings.title: Cross-stage resources and optional offers alter available strategies
findings.finding: Resources carry with capacity two and special refills compete with ordinary items. At one remaining C05 token, fee two spends one while reach remains empowered, so acceleration cannot be assumed. Complete acquisition ranking and no-tool/no-refill continuations are absent. Reserves require additional ownership/timing or operative-cost prerequisites.
